the bridge dylibs themselves are NOT byte-reproducible: `make deps` rebuilds the static closures from scratch and the resulting archives (and therefore the linked dylibs) differ on every run. the IPA sha256 is not a stable anchor: the zip records file mtimes, so re-patching the same input yields a different artifact digest while packaged_main_sha256 and the dylib hashes stay the same. Use packaged_main_sha256 for regression anchors.

root cause: `npabridge/payload.py` emitted the dladdr result check as `cbnz w0, publish_old`, but dladdr reports success with a non-zero result, so a successful lookup was treated as a failure; the basename scan also stopped at the first '/', so an absolute dli_fname could never match its basename. Both were present since the first payload commit b146213, so the dispatch had never activated

fix: test the dladdr result with CBZ and compare the final path component (the scan reaches the NUL, then steps back over the basename and requires the preceding byte to be '/'). `npabridge.payload` now asserts both shapes on every assembly

runtime proof: macOS PlayCover, iPhone-SE-class app, installed bundle carrying the fixed payload. Before the fix the libass unit state word read 3 (OLD) while LibASSBridge.dylib was loaded and dlsym returned its symbol; after the fix the three unit state words read 2 (NEW) and every slot holds a bridge address
libass 0.17.5 behaviour confirmed visually: the \kt probe renders the 0.17 karaoke behaviour (libass only added the \kt override tag in 0.17.0), where the bundled 0.13.7 ignores it
